candidates.description: req.body.id is passed directly as a MongoDB query filter in updateProductReviews without type validation or ownership check, and multi:true allows mass updates.
candidates.rationale: Line 18 uses req.body.id as the _id filter in db.reviewsCollection.update with multi:true. No ObjectId validation or user-ownership check exists. A crafted JSON body like {"id":{"$ne":null},"message":"x"} would update all reviews. Verification: send a POST with a NoSQL operator payload as id and observe multi-document modification.
candidates.title: NoSQL injection in review update via unsanitized req.body.id

candidates.description: req.body.key is concatenated into a file path for fs.readFileSync without sanitization, allowing directory traversal to read arbitrary YAML files.
candidates.rationale: Line 80-81 builds a path as './data/static/codefixes/' + key + '.info.yml' where key comes from req.body.key (line 71). No path normalization or allowlist check is applied. A key like '../../../package.json' would read outside the intended directory. Verification: POST a key containing ../ sequences and check if file content is reflected in the response.
candidates.title: Path traversal in vulnCodeFixes via req.body.key in file read

candidates.description: retrieveBasket fetches any basket by req.params.id without verifying the authenticated user owns it; the challenge detection code proves the gap but does not block access.
candidates.rationale: Line 19 queries BasketModel.findOne by id from req.params with no ownership filter. Lines 21-23 only detect the IDOR for challenge scoring via challengeUtils.solveIf but do not return 403 or filter results. Any authenticated user can read another user's basket. Verification: authenticate as user A, request /rest/basket/{B_id}, confirm basket contents are returned.
candidates.title: IDOR in basket retrieval without ownership enforcement
